headline: Copypasta About Fake Medical Condition Now Being Cited as Real by Patients
subheadline: Doctors report influx of patients claiming symptoms from satirical text post
summary: A satirical copypasta describing a fake medical condition has been taken seriously by enough people to cause medical consultation increases.
content:
Doctors are reporting an increase in patients presenting with symptoms of "Chronic Awareness Syndrome"—a condition that does not exist and was invented as part of a satirical copypasta post in 2022.

The original copypasta, which has been shared millions of times, reads: "I have been diagnosed with Chronic Awareness Syndrome (CAS). Symptoms include: being constantly aware that you are breathing, noticing when you blink, feeling your tongue in your mouth, and an inability to find a comfortable resting position for your arms. There is no cure. Only awareness."

The post was clearly intended as humor, describing common experiences reframed as a medical condition. But doctors report patients citing it as legitimate.

"I had three patients this month claim to have CAS," said Dr. Amanda Foster. "They described the symptoms exactly as written in the copypasta. When I explained it's not real, two of them insisted I was 'not up on the latest research.'"

The phenomenon illustrates how information spreads and mutates online. The copypasta has been copied without the original satirical context, shared in wellness forums as genuine, and even discussed in support groups for undiagnosed conditions.

"It reads like a real condition," explained one patient who requested the diagnosis. "The symptoms are specific. It has a name. Why would someone make that up?"

Medical professionals have attempted to debunk the myth, but new believers emerge faster than corrections spread. The copypasta has been translated into 14 languages, each iteration losing more satirical markers.

"This is how misinformation works," noted Dr. Foster. "Something starts as an obvious joke. It spreads. Context disappears. Eventually, someone's genuinely asking their doctor about Chronic Awareness Syndrome."

At press time, 847 posts on health forums discussed CAS as real. One support group had formed. Their slogan: "You're not alone. You're just aware."

The original copypasta author could not be reached for comment and probably never expected to be.
author: Sandra Mitchell, Health & Technology
